correctness.rationale: For each pair X of ground vertices, total domination is equivalent to no two-vertex transversal of the selected ground edges. On four selected edges a triangle either forces a two-cover or yields an induced star without a perfect matching. Otherwise the four-edge graph is bipartite, so Koenig vertex-cover/matching duality yields a three-edge matching. Conversely such a matching plus any fourth edge is paired dominating. The three support types have independently counted 180/315/105 labeled realizations per selected six/seven/eight ground vertices. One-edge matching replacements produce shared reconfiguration states and two-edge matching flips produce adjacent states; elementary support changes and perfect-matching flips connect all three-matchings. The two standalone finite checkers recompute four-subset feasibility through order ten and reconfiguration connectivity through order nine, but the proofs cover all n>=6.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text examination of the two relevant Kneser-domination papers confirms that their minimum ordinary, tuple and total domination theorems do not determine the present four-element paired-minimum counts, the multiplicities of induced perfect matchings or one-token reconfiguration connectivity. Dedicated database searches for the exact family, three-matching characterization, and mobility found no matching published record. Known three-edge-matching total-dominating sets are acknowledged as prior context, not claimed as new. The new matched four-set census and connected configuration-space theorem are separately proved.
residual_risks: An unindexed or inaccessible work might already contain an equivalent paired-domination census or reconfiguration proof.

The prior total-domination structure supplies a close starting point; part of the enumeration can be obtained using straightforward finite matching-type counting, but reconfiguration connectivity and the full paired classification require the supplied structural arguments.
The n=5 boundary is outside the theorem; finite verification is not a substitute for its general proof.

value.rationale: The paired matching condition refines the previously studied total-domination condition on a canonical highly symmetric family. The theorem gives all optimal solutions, exact support-orbit multiplicities, their induced perfect-matching multiplicities, and a constructive connectivity theorem showing the solution space has no token-jumping obstruction at any ground-set size n>=6. These are precise natural invariants unavailable from the known scalar total-domination result, and may inform exchange-based placement and optimal-set enumeration.
